candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the applicable limit and reported measurement are compared on a geometric-mean basis, and whether units are ug/l/ppb or another specified unit, changes which numeric limit applies and whether a reported value is commensurate for exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Substituting one-half the detection limit when DL exceeds MQL yields a numeric effluent value for limit comparison instead of treating the result as non-numeric or missing, which can change whether an enforceable limit comparison is performed and how censored results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When DL is below MQL, treating the result as no data rather than a numeric substitute prevents limit exceedance comparison and shifts the case toward documented no-data or missing-evidence semantics rather than a compliance determination.

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The discretionary choice between the reported censored value and zero changes the numeric effluent input used for limit comparison and whether the evidence is treated as a qualifying measurement, a zero result, or an unresolved no-data state.

Different readings of the instream waste concentration formula, its inputs, or the embedded 2.13 factor change the calculated concentration that may be compared against water quality criteria when determining applicable discharge limits.

candidates.exact_span: F    = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is referenced externally rather than fixed in this segment; different interpretations of the applicable F value change Cd and therefore which numeric criterion or limit governs the discharge evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting 4Q3 versus harmonic mean for Qa changes dilution in the Cd calculation and can change which instream concentration—and thus which applicable numeric limit—is produced for human health criteria.

candidates.exact_span: The following formular convert metals reported in total form to dissolved form if criteria are in dissolved form
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether total-reported metals must be converted to dissolved form before comparison determines which dissolved criteria apply and whether a reported total measurement is evaluated against the correct enforceable numeric limit.

Interpretation of the dissolved-fraction conversion, including TSS source and exponent handling, changes the dissolved metal concentration derived from total measurements and therefore the applicable limit for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS is taken from the receiving stream or from effluent for intermittent streams changes Kp and dissolved-metal conversion, which can change the numeric limit deemed applicable to a total metal measurement.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Application of the low-pH aluminum acute criterion override replaces the hardness-derived acute value with a fixed 750 ug/l limit, changing which enforceable numeric acute limit applies.

candidates.exact_span: If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: Application of the low-pH aluminum chronic criterion override replaces the hardness-derived chronic value with a fixed 87 ug/l limit, changing which enforceable numeric chronic limit applies.
The hardness-correction factor CF1 changes the calculated acute cadmium criterion, so different hardness values or formula interpretation change the applicable acute discharge limit.
The hardness-correction factor CF2 changes the calculated chronic cadmium criterion, so different hardness values or formula interpretation change the applicable chronic discharge limit.
